question: The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium, the largest hockey stadium in the country, is situated in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rourkela, Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium is located in Rourkela, Odisha, and with a seating capacity of about 21,000, it is regarded as the largest hockey stadium in the world. (बिरसा मुंडा हॉकी स्टेडियम — राउरकेला, ओडिशा)

 

• It was built to host the FIH Odisha Hockey Men's World Cup 2023 (co-hosted with Bhubaneswar) and is named after the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda.

 

• Odisha has emerged as a major hub for Indian hockey and has been the title sponsor of the Indian national hockey teams since 2018.

 

• Rourkela is also the home town of hockey legend Dilip Tirkey, and the stadium was inaugurated in November 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhubaneswar's Kalinga Stadium also co-hosted matches of the 2023 Hockey World Cup, having earlier hosted the 2018 edition solo.

 

• Odisha has hosted the Hockey World Cup twice in a row — 2018 (Bhubaneswar) and 2023 (Bhubaneswar-Rourkela).

 

NOTE

 

• Bhubaneswar, Odisha (Option 1): Home to the Kalinga Stadium, a major hockey venue, but not the stadium described as the country's largest.

 

• Jharsuguda, Odisha (Option 2): Known chiefly for the Veer Surendra Sai Airport, not for a major hockey stadium.

 

• Cuttack, Odisha (Option 3): Known for the Barabati Stadium, primarily a cricket venue.

question: Which of the following is NOT a subdivision of the Meghalaya plateau?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhansiri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Meghalaya Plateau (also called the Shillong Plateau), an extension of the Peninsular Plateau, is traditionally divided into three hill regions: the Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills, and Garo Hills. (मेघालय पठार — खासी, जयंतिया, गारो पहाड़ियाँ)

 

• Dhansiri refers to a river and valley located mainly in Assam and Nagaland; it is not part of the Meghalaya plateau's subdivisions.

 

• The Meghalaya plateau is separated from the main Chotanagpur plateau by a fault called the Malda Gap, and from the Mikir Hills of Assam by the Kopili river valley.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khasi Hills contain Shillong (state capital) and Mawsynram/Cherrapunji, among the wettest places on Earth.

 

• The Garo Hills are home to the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO Man and Biosphere Reserve.

 

NOTE

 

• Khasi (Option 1): A genuine hill subdivision of the Meghalaya plateau.

 

• Jaintia (Option 2): A genuine hill subdivision of the Meghalaya plateau.

 

• Garo (Option 3): A genuine hill subdivision of the Meghalaya plateau.

question: Which period in India is described as Plan Holiday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1966 to 1969.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The period from 1966 to 1969 is called the Plan Holiday in India's planning history. (योजना अवकाश — 1966-1969)

 

• After the failure of the Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66) — caused by the Indo-China War (1962), Indo-Pak War (1965), and severe droughts — annual plans were adopted instead of a fixed five-year plan for these three years.

 

• During this period, emphasis shifted to agriculture and allied sectors, which also coincided with the launch of the Green Revolution.

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan began only in 1969, after the Plan Holiday ended.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, ending the era of Five-Year Plans after the Twelfth Plan (2012-17).

 

NOTE

 

• 1990 to 1993 (Option 1): This period also saw plan disruption (Eighth Plan delayed to 1992-97) due to political instability and the 1991 economic crisis, but it is not called the "Plan Holiday".

 

• 1956 to 1960 (Option 3): This falls within the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), based on the Mahalanobis model.

 

• 1947 to 1950 (Option 4): This was the pre-Plan period, before the Planning Commission was set up in 1950.

question: What is the percentage horizontal reservation for women in the government jobs bill of Uttarakhand, approved by Governor Gurmit Singh on January 10, 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 10 January 2023, Uttarakhand Governor Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Gurmit Singh gave assent to the Uttarakhand Public Service (Horizontal Reservation for Women) Act, 2022, granting 30% horizontal reservation to women domiciled in the state in government jobs. (उत्तराखंड महिला क्षैतिज आरक्षण — 30%)

 

• The reservation is horizontal, meaning it cuts across all vertical categories (General, OBC, SC, ST) rather than being a separate additional quota.

 

• The bill was passed by the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly in the Winter Session of 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Several other states, including Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, also provide horizontal reservation for women in government jobs, though the percentages differ by state.

 

NOTE

 

• 40% (Option 2), 20% (Option 3), 50% (Option 4): These figures do not match the reservation percentage actually notified under the Uttarakhand Act, which is fixed at 30%.

question: Who among the following Indian female boxers won the gold medal in the 1st Edition of Elorda Boxing Cup 2022 held in Kazakhstan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alfiya Pathan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian boxer Alfiya Pathan won a gold medal at the 1st Elorda Boxing Cup 2022, held in Astana, Kazakhstan, defeating a former world champion in her category. (एलोर्डा बॉक्सिंग कप 2022 — अल्फिया पठान)

 

• Fellow Indian boxer Gitika also won a gold medal at the same edition; India finished the tournament with a total of 14 medals.

 

• The Elorda Cup is a prestigious international boxing tournament hosted annually in Kazakhstan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nikhat Zareen and Minakshi won gold medals for India at a later edition of the Elorda Cup (2024), not the 1st edition in 2022.

 

• Mary Kom and Lovlina Borgohain are both decorated Indian boxers with Olympic medals but were not the gold medallists at the 1st Elorda Cup 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Nikhat Zareen (Option 1): She won gold at the Elorda Cup in a later (2024) edition, not the 1st edition referred to here.

 

• Mary Kom (Option 2): A six-time World Champion boxer, but not the gold medallist at this particular event.

 

• Lovlina Borgohain (Option 4): An Olympic bronze medallist (Tokyo 2020) in boxing, but not the gold medallist at this event.

question: Who described Indian federal system as a bargaining federalism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Morris Jones.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• British political scientist W.H. Morris-Jones described the Indian federal system as "bargaining federalism", highlighting the constant negotiation between the Centre and the States. (सौदेबाजी संघवाद — मॉरिस जोन्स)

 

• He characterised Centre-State relations in India as a continuous process of political bargaining rather than a rigid, legally fixed division of power.

 

• This concept emphasises the cooperative and negotiated nature of Indian federalism, as opposed to a strictly "holding-together" or "coming-together" federal model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• K. Santhanam described Indian federalism in terms of Centre-State financial relations, while Paul Appleby called Indian administration "one of the great governmental systems of the world".

 

• India is often described as a "quasi-federal" state or having a "federation with a unitary bias".

 

NOTE

 

• KC Wheare (Option 1): Described the Indian Constitution as establishing a system of government which is "quasi-federal", not as "bargaining federalism".

 

• Ivor Jennings (Option 2): Called the Indian Constitution "a federation with a strong centralising tendency".

 

• Granville Austin (Option 3): Described Indian federalism as "cooperative federalism", terming India's Constitution as one of "cooperative federalism".

question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of national income from broader to narrower concepts?
option_1: GNP at market prices – NNP at market prices – GNP at factor cost – NNP at factor cost
option_2: Personal disposable income – Personal income – GNP at market prices – GNP at factor cost
option_3: GNP at factor cost – GNP at market prices – NNP at market prices – Personal income
option_4: GNP at factor cost – NNP at factor cost – Personal income – Personal disposable income
solution_text:
The correct answer is GNP at factor cost – NNP at factor cost – Personal income – Personal disposable income.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The standard broader-to-narrower sequence of national income aggregates is: GNP at factor cost → NNP at factor cost (National Income) → Personal Income → Personal Disposable Income. (राष्ट्रीय आय अवधारणाएँ — जीएनपी से व्यक्तिगत disposable आय तक)

 

• GNP at factor cost is the broadest, since NNP at factor cost = GNP at factor cost − Depreciation, making NNP fc narrower than GNP fc.

 

• NNP at factor cost is also called National Income; Personal Income = National Income − undistributed profits − corporate tax − social security contributions + transfer payments, making it narrower still.

 

• Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − direct personal taxes, the narrowest of the four, representing income actually available to households for consumption/saving.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• GDP differs from GNP by excluding net factor income from abroad; NDP differs from GDP by excluding depreciation.

 

• Market price valuations include net indirect taxes, while factor cost valuations reflect returns actually received by factors of production.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Mixes market-price and factor-cost concepts inconsistently without a valid broader-to-narrower logic connecting all four terms.

 

• Option 2: Reverses the order, starting from the narrowest concept (Personal Disposable Income) instead of the broadest.

 

• Option 3: Places GNP at factor cost before GNP at market prices, which is incorrect since GNP at factor cost is derived from GNP at market prices by removing net indirect taxes, not the other way in this broader-narrower sense used here.

question: Laho is the dance form of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Laho is a popular folk dance of the Pnar (Jaintia) community of Meghalaya, performed during harvest festivals. (लाहो नृत्य — मेघालय)

 

• It is performed in a circle by men and women together, marked by rhythmic footwork and singing, and is associated with festivity and community bonding.

 

• It is closely linked to the Jaintia Hills region of Meghalaya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Meghalaya include Wangala (harvest dance of the Garo tribe, also called the "Hundred Drums Festival") and Shad Suk Mynsiem (Khasi thanksgiving dance).

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for classical Manipuri dance and folk forms like Thang-Ta, not Laho.

 

• Sikkim (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Chu Faat Dance and Singhi Chham, not Laho.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for classical dance forms like Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, not Laho.

question: The musical instrument Sarod is associated with:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amjad Ali Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is one of India's most renowned sarod players, belonging to the Senia Bangash gharana. (सरोद — उस्ताद अमजद अली खान)

 

• He is a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan and has been instrumental in popularising the sarod internationally.

 

• Other legendary sarod exponents include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, considered a pioneer of the instrument in the modern era.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The sarod is a fretless stringed instrument, believed to have evolved from the Afghan rabab.

 

NOTE

 

• Zakir Hussain (Option 1): A world-renowned tabla player, not associated with the sarod.

 

• Allahrakha (Option 2): A legendary tabla maestro (guru of Zakir Hussain), not associated with the sarod.

 

• Khayyam (Option 4): A celebrated Indian music director for films, not a sarod player.

question: Which of the following programmes was launched by NABARD in 2015 to promote the livelihood of the people in both farm and off-farm activities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is LEDP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• LEDP (Livelihood and Enterprise Development Programme) was launched by NABARD in 2015 to promote sustainable livelihoods through skill-based training in both farm and off-farm activities. (LEDP — नाबार्ड की आजीविका एवं उद्यम विकास योजना)

 

• It focuses on providing hands-on skill training to rural people (particularly those linked with SHGs) to enable them to take up income-generating activities.

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established in 1982 to promote sustainable and equitable agriculture and rural development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD also runs the MEDP (Micro Enterprise Development Programme), a related but separate skill-training scheme.

 

• NABARD's other key initiatives include the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) and the Kisan Credit Card scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• LWE (Option 1): Refers to Left Wing Extremism, an internal security concern, unrelated to NABARD's livelihood programmes.

 

• MEDP (Option 3): A genuine NABARD skill-development scheme (Micro Enterprise Development Programme), but it was not the one launched specifically in 2015 as described.

 

• BLP (Option 4): Not a recognised NABARD livelihood programme matching this description.

question: Which of the following teams won the Raja Bhalindra Singh trophy at the 36th National Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Services.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Services sports team won the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy, awarded to the overall champion, at the 36th National Games 2022 held in Gujarat. (राजा भालिंद्र सिंह ट्रॉफी — सर्विसेज)

 

• This was Services' fourth consecutive Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy win, topping the medals tally with the highest number of gold medals.

 

• The 36th National Games were held from 29 September to 12 October 2022 across multiple venues in Gujarat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy is named after Yadavindra Singh, former Maharaja of Patiala and a long-time president of the Indian Olympic Association.

 

• Host state Gujarat achieved its best-ever performance at these Games, finishing among the top medal-winning states.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2), Maharashtra (Option 3), Punjab (Option 4): All performed creditably at the 36th National Games and won multiple medals, but none of them won the overall Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy, which went to Services.

question: Which of the following is a festival and dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bihu is both a major harvest festival and a traditional folk dance of Assam. (बिहू — पर्व और नृत्य दोनों, असम)

 

• There are three Bihu festivals celebrated annually — Rongali/Bohag Bihu (spring), Kongali/Kati Bihu (autumn), and Bhogali/Magh Bihu (winter harvest) — each accompanied by energetic Bihu dance performances.

 

• Bihu dance is performed by young men and women in colourful traditional attire, accompanied by instruments like the dhol, pepa, and taal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rongali Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and the beginning of the sowing season, usually celebrated in mid-April.

 

NOTE

 

• Baisakhi (Option 1): A harvest festival of Punjab; the associated dance forms are Bhangra (male) and Giddha (female), which are named separately, not simply called "Baisakhi".

 

• Ugadi (Option 2): A New Year festival celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka, without a dance form named after it.

 

• Pongal (Option 3): A harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, without a dance form named after it.

question: Which organic chemical compound is reacted with nitrous acid at 273-278K to prepare benzenediazonium chloride?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aniline.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aniline (C6H5NH2) reacts with nitrous acid (HNO2, generated in situ from NaNO2 + HCl) at a low temperature of 273-278 K (0-5°C) to form benzenediazonium chloride through a process called diazotisation. (डाइएज़ोटीकरण अभिक्रिया — एनिलीन से बेंज़ीनडाइएज़ोनियम क्लोराइड)

 

• The reaction: C6H5NH2 + NaNO2 + 2HCl → C6H5N2+Cl− + NaCl + 2H2O.

 

• Low temperature is essential because diazonium salts are unstable above 5°C and decompose readily, especially in aqueous solution at higher temperatures.

 

• Benzenediazonium chloride is a key intermediate used to synthesise a variety of aromatic compounds, dyes, and other organic compounds via coupling and substitution reactions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diazonium salts undergo azo coupling reactions to form azo dyes, widely used in the textile industry.

 

• The Sandmeyer reaction uses diazonium salts to introduce halogens or cyanide groups into the benzene ring.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrazine (Option 1): N2H4, a reducing agent and rocket fuel component, not used to prepare benzenediazonium chloride.

 

• Toluene (Option 2): A methylbenzene without an amino group; it cannot undergo diazotisation since diazotisation requires a primary aromatic amine.

 

• Pyridine (Option 4): A heterocyclic aromatic amine used as a solvent/base, not a primary aromatic amine and hence not used in this diazotisation reaction.

question: Balban served as naib to which of the following sultans of Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nasiruddin Mahmud.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban served as Naib-i-Mamlakat (deputy of the kingdom) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty, before ascending the throne himself in 1266 CE. (नायब — नासिरुद्दीन महमूद के अधीन बलबन)

 

• Balban was originally one of the Chalisa/Chihalgani (the "Forty"), a group of powerful Turkic nobles under Iltutmish, and later rose to become the most powerful noble under Nasiruddin Mahmud.

 

• He effectively controlled the administration as naib during Nasiruddin Mahmud's reign and succeeded him as Sultan after his death.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As Sultan, Balban is known for his "Blood and Iron" policy, strengthening the crown's authority and crushing the power of the Chalisa nobles.

 

• He introduced Persian court customs like sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the sultan's feet).

 

NOTE

 

• Iltutmish (Option 1): The Sultan who originally brought Balban into royal service as a member of the Chalisa, but Balban was not his naib.

 

• Razia (Option 2): Iltutmish's daughter and successor as Sultan; Balban was not her naib.

 

• Qutb ud-Din Aibak (Option 4): Founder of the Slave Dynasty and Iltutmish's predecessor; Balban did not serve as his naib.

question: Which of the following are cryptogam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pteridophyta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cryptogams are flowerless, seedless plants that reproduce through spores, and include algae, fungi, bryophytes, and pteridophytes (ferns). (क्रिप्टोगैम — पुष्पविहीन, बीजरहित पौधे जैसे टेरिडोफाइटा)

 

• Pteridophyta (e.g., ferns) reproduce via spores and lack seeds and flowers, placing them firmly in the cryptogam group.

 

• The term "cryptogam" literally means "hidden reproduction", as opposed to phanerogams (seed plants) whose reproductive organs are visible as flowers/cones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cryptogams are traditionally divided into Thallophyta (algae), Bryophyta (mosses/liverworts), and Pteridophyta (ferns).

 

• Phanerogams (seed-bearing plants) are divided into Gymnosperms (naked seeds) and Angiosperms (seeds enclosed in fruit).

 

NOTE

 

• Gymnosperm (Option 1): A phanerogam (seed-bearing plant) with naked, unenclosed seeds — not a cryptogam.

 

• Dicots (Option 2): A subclass of angiosperms, which are seed-bearing phanerogams — not a cryptogam.

 

• Angiosperm (Option 3): A phanerogam bearing seeds enclosed within a fruit — not a cryptogam.

question: What is the name of the two small moons orbiting Mars discovered by American astronomer Asaph Hall in 1877?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phobos and Deimos.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The two small natural satellites of Mars, named Phobos and Deimos, were discovered by American astronomer Asaph Hall in 1877 at the US Naval Observatory. (फोबोस और डीमोस — मंगल ग्रह के दो चंद्रमा)

 

• They are named after the mythological Greek twin gods of fear and terror (sons of Ares/Mars), fitting companions for the "Red Planet".

 

• Both moons are irregularly shaped and very small; Phobos is the larger and closer of the two, orbiting Mars in less than 8 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Scientists believe Phobos and Deimos may be captured asteroids from the nearby asteroid belt, rather than moons formed alongside Mars.

 

• Phobos is gradually spiralling inward and is predicted to eventually break apart or crash into Mars.

 

NOTE

 

• Miranda and Triton (Option 2): Miranda is a moon of Uranus, and Triton is a moon of Neptune — neither belongs to Mars.

 

• Enceladus and Titan (Option 3): Both are moons of Saturn, not Mars.

 

• Charon and Dysnomia (Option 4): Charon is a moon of the dwarf planet Pluto, and Dysnomia is a moon of the dwarf planet Eris — neither belongs to Mars.

question:
In December 2022, Meghana Ahlawat was elected as the

President of _________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Table Tennis Federation of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meghna Ahlawat was elected as the President of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) in December 2022, becoming the first woman to hold this position. (टेबल टेनिस फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडिया — मेघना अहलावत)

 

• Former table tennis player and eight-time national champion Kamlesh Mehta was elected as the Secretary General of TTFI in the same election.

 

• TTFI is the governing body for table tennis in India, affiliated with the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's top table tennis players include Manika Batra, Sharath Kamal, and Sathiyan Gnanasekaran.

 

NOTE

 

• BCCI (Option 2): The Board of Control for Cricket in India; its president at the time was Roger Binny, not Meghna Ahlawat.

 

• Hockey India (Option 3): The governing body for hockey in India, headed by different officials, unrelated to this election.

 

• Wrestling Federation of India (Option 4): The governing body for wrestling in India, headed by different officials, unrelated to this election.

question: _________ connect India's four big metro cities of Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golden Quadrilateral.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) is a network of highways connecting India's four largest metro cities — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata — forming a quadrilateral shape. (गोल्डन क्वाड्रीलेटरल — दिल्ली-मुंबई-चेन्नई-कोलकाता)

 

• It is the largest highway project in India, spanning about 5,846 km, and was developed under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).

 

• The project was launched in 1999 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and executed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-South and East-West Corridor is a separate NHDP project connecting Srinagar to Kanyakumari and Silchar to Porbandar.

 

• NHDP was launched in phases, of which the Golden Quadrilateral was Phase I and II's flagship component.

 

NOTE

 

• North-South Corridor of NHDP (Option 1): Connects Srinagar (north) to Kanyakumari (south), not the four metro cities in a quadrilateral.

 

• National Highway 44 (Option 2): India's longest national highway, running north-south from Srinagar to Kanyakumari, not connecting the four metro cities as a quadrilateral.

 

• National Highway 47A (Option 3): A short highway connecting Kochi city to NH 47, unrelated to the metro city connectivity described.

question: Who became the first Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1969?
solution_text:
The correct answer is G Parthasarathi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• G. Parthasarathi became the first Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) when it was established in 1969. (जेएनयू के प्रथम कुलपति — जी पार्थसारथी)

 

• JNU was established by an Act of Parliament, the Jawaharlal Nehru University Act, 1966, and named after India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

• G. Parthasarathi was a noted diplomat and academician who also served as India's ambassador to several countries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• JNU is located in New Delhi and is well known for its schools of social sciences, international studies, and languages.

 

• Former President K.R. Narayanan later served as a professor at JNU's School of International Studies before entering politics.

 

NOTE

 

• BD Nagchaudhuri (Option 1): A physicist who served as JNU's Vice-Chancellor at a later period, not the first.

 

• Y Nayudamma (Option 3): A noted scientist and former Director General of CSIR, not associated with JNU's founding vice-chancellorship.

 

• KR Narayanan (Option 4): Later served as a professor at JNU and became President of India, but was never JNU's Vice-Chancellor.

question: Who among the following received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award of 2019 in the Kathakali classical dance category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kottakkal Nandakumaran Nair.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kottakkal Nandakumaran Nair, a renowned Kathakali artist popularly known as "Kathakali Ashaan", received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2019 in the Kathakali category. (कथकली — कोट्टक्कल नंदकुमारन नायर)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) is India's highest award for practising artists in the fields of music, dance, and drama, conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy of music, dance, and drama.

 

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and codified gestures (mudras).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, headquartered in New Delhi, was established in 1952 as India's first National Academy for the arts.

 

• Awards for 2019, 2020, and 2021 were announced together by the Akademi due to delays.

 

NOTE

 

• OS Arun (Option 1): A well-known Carnatic vocalist, not a Kathakali exponent.

 

• Manju Nandan Mehta (Option 2): Not associated with the Kathakali award for 2019.

 

• Vinayak Torvi (Option 4): A noted Hindustani classical vocalist, not a Kathakali dancer.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which state in India has the lowest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of India 2011, Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among all Indian states, at approximately 63.82%. (जनगणना 2011 — सबसे कम साक्षरता दर, बिहार)

 

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate in the same census, at approximately 93.91%.

 

• Low literacy in Bihar has historically been linked to factors such as high poverty levels, limited access to educational infrastructure, and gender gaps in education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, India's overall literacy rate was 74.04% (male: 82.14%, female: 65.46%).

 

• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep had one of the highest literacy rates.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Had a relatively low literacy rate (around 66.4%) but higher than Bihar's, so it was not the lowest.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Had a literacy rate of around 66.1%, higher than Bihar's, so it was not the lowest.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 4): Had a literacy rate of around 65.4%, higher than Bihar's, so it was not the lowest.

question: Who issues ₹10 notes in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), India's central bank, has the sole authority to issue currency notes of all denominations, including the ₹10 note, under the RBI Act, 1934. (₹10 का नोट — भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा जारी)

 

• The only exception is the ₹1 note and coins, which are issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance), though even the ₹1 note is circulated through the RBI.

 

• The RBI Governor's signature appears on all notes issued by the RBI, from ₹2 up to ₹2000 (as applicable).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission, and was nationalised in 1949.

 

• RBI's currency-issuing function is carried out under the Issue Department, backed by the Minimum Reserve System.

 

NOTE

 

• State Bank of India (Option 2): India's largest public sector commercial bank, but it does not issue currency notes.

 

• Union Bank of India (Option 3): A public sector commercial bank, but it does not issue currency notes.

 

• Central Bank of India (Option 4): A public sector commercial bank (despite its name), but it is not India's central bank and does not issue currency notes.

question: Which of these is NOT the correctly stated component of the expenditure method of measuring national income?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Export plus import expenditure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the expenditure method of measuring national income, National Income = Final Consumption Expenditure by households (C) + Final Investment Expenditure by firms (I) + Final Government Expenditure (G) + Net Exports (X − M). (व्यय विधि — शुद्ध निर्यात, न कि निर्यात + आयात)

 

• The correctly stated foreign trade component is "exports minus imports" (net exports), not "exports plus imports".

 

• Adding exports and imports (instead of subtracting) would incorrectly inflate the national income figure, since imports represent expenditure on goods/services not produced domestically and must be netted out, not added.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The expenditure method is one of three main approaches to measuring national income — the other two being the product (output) method and the income method.

 

• Net exports (X − M) can be negative when a country's imports exceed its exports, reducing measured national income.

 

NOTE

 

• Final investment expenditure by firms (Option 1): A correctly stated component of the expenditure method.

 

• Final government expenditure (Option 2): A correctly stated component of the expenditure method.

 

• Final consumption expenditure by households (Option 4): A correctly stated component of the expenditure method.

question: What is the IUPAC name of allylamine which is used to make pharmaceuticals and other chemicals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2-Propen-1-amine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Allylamine (CH2=CH-CH2-NH2) has the IUPAC name 2-Propen-1-amine (or prop-2-en-1-amine), reflecting a three-carbon chain with a double bond at C2 and an amine group at C1. (एलिलामाइन — 2-प्रोपेन-1-अमीन)

 

• Allylamine is an unsaturated primary amine, used as a starting material in the synthesis of various pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and polymers.

 

• IUPAC nomenclature for amines names the parent hydrocarbon chain and adds the suffix "-amine" at the position of the -NH2 group, retaining the ene/yne unsaturation locant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Allylamine is manufactured industrially mainly from allyl chloride and ammonia, or from acrolein via reductive amination.

 

• It is a highly reactive, flammable, and toxic liquid with a pungent, ammonia-like odour.

 

NOTE

 

• Propan-1-amine (Option 1): This is the IUPAC name for n-propylamine (CH3CH2CH2NH2), a saturated amine, not allylamine.

 

• Benzenamine (Option 2): This is the IUPAC name for aniline (C6H5NH2), an aromatic amine, not allylamine.

 

• N-Methylethanamine (Option 3): This is the IUPAC name for a secondary amine, N-methylethylamine (CH3CH2NHCH3), not allylamine.

question: The idea of concurrent list in the Indian Constitution was taken from _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idea of the Concurrent List, containing subjects on which both the Union and State governments can legislate, was borrowed from the Constitution of Australia. (समवर्ती सूची — ऑस्ट्रेलिया से प्रेरित)

 

• The Indian Constitution's Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers into three lists — Union List, State List, and Concurrent List — a scheme largely inspired by the Government of India Act, 1935, with the Concurrent List concept itself traced to Australia.

 

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law generally prevails (Article 254).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• From the Australian Constitution, India also borrowed concepts like the freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse and the idea of a joint sitting of Parliament.

 

• From Germany, India borrowed the provision for the suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency.

 

NOTE

 

• Germany (Option 1): The source of the Emergency provisions (suspension of Fundamental Rights), not the Concurrent List.

 

• Denmark (Option 3): Not a source of any major borrowed feature of the Indian Constitution; not linked to the Concurrent List.

 

• Ireland (Option 4): The source of the Directive Principles of State Policy and the method of election of the President, not the Concurrent List.
